title: Standard Entropies Can Be Used to Calculate Entropy Changes of Chemical Reactions
lead: A table of standard molar entropies gives the entropy change of a reaction without following the reaction itself, because entropy depends only on the state. The combustion of methane is the worked case.
exercise_notes: The book sets no exercise on this section, so the exercise, its solution, Bloom level and concept tags are written by AI. The numeric answer accepts a 2% tolerance.

exercises.source_id: look at the combustion of methane
exercises.prompt: Use the table of standard entropies to find $\Delta_{rxn}S^\circ$ for the reverse of the combustion, $2\,\mathrm{H_2O}(g) + \mathrm{CO_2}(g) \rightarrow \mathrm{CH_4}(g) + 2\,\mathrm{O_2}(g)$.

answer.solution: $\Delta_{rxn}S^\circ = [1(186.25) + 2(205.15)] - [2(188.84) + 1(213.79)] = 596.55 - 591.47 = +5.08$ J/(mol·K). Reversing a reaction swaps its products and reactants, so $\Delta_{rxn}S^\circ$ keeps its size and changes sign.

footnotes.html: The table gives 213.79 J/(mol·K) for $\mathrm{CO_2}$, and the sum printed below uses 213.70. With 213.79 the result is −5.08 J/(mol·K).
